about: Lesson A7 (a07-flexible-demand). Prairie Town is fictional: the flexible share, the losses, the users' cost, the devices, their counts and ratings, the values, the coordination cost, Feeder 7 and the neighbours are illustrative. The day is 9 June 2025 on real Southwest Power Pool shapes (EIA-930 in town_year.json), cut and scaled as lesson 9, CF6 and A4 do; each hour is dispatched cheapest first (the town's 100 MW always-on plant, wind and sun, the combined-cycle plant at $40/MWh and 0.37 t CO2/MWh, the peaker at $100/MWh and 0.55 t CO2/MWh; CO2 at the plant only). The real-world box quotes two cited papers word for word; _tests/learn/test_a07-flexible-demand.js checks every number on the page.

shift.note: Illustrative: each hour's use may move up or down by at most the flexible share of that hour's demand; the day's total stays the same, plus 10% extra energy when it is on (each MWh moved needs 1.1 MWh at its new hour, as when a home is pre-cooled: about 9% of what arrives is lost). The users' cost moves in steps of $6 a MWh, so no setting makes a move save exactly nothing (at $40, $56 or $60 a move would tie, and the plants' CO2 would no longer be the same in every least-cost shift).

devices.name: Home batteries
devices.note: 13.5 kWh each, keeping 20% for a power cut: 3.6 kW for three hours; refilled, without losses here, from the next day's spare sun.

devices.name: Smart thermostats
devices.note: Air conditioning set a few degrees warmer: 1.2 kW less; 70% of homes take part; 80% of the skipped energy comes back as the homes cool down.

devices.name: EV chargers
devices.note: 7 kW each; 40% are plugged in and charging during the event; all the skipped charging comes back.

devices.name: Dairies' pumps
devices.note: Irrigation and milk-cooling pumps, 300 kW a farm; the milk is chilled ahead and the fields watered later.

vpp.note: Illustrative: the aggregator is paid $50 per kW a year for being ready, plus the running cost its devices save the town on 30 event days a year like 9 June 2025; it keeps 20% and pays a coordination cost for each device or farm (meters, software, customer service).

feeder.name: Feeder 7
feeder.note: Illustrative: a feeder for 1,000 homes rated 3.0 MW, its load following the town's shape with its own peak of 3.0 MW at 17:00.

trade.note: Illustrative: under net billing the solar home's midday kWh earn the hour's running cost, $0 on 9 June; its neighbour, the renter, is on A4's real-time tariff, so in those hours it pays the hour's price, $0, plus A4's plant-and-wire charge, 9.5¢ per kWh (not A4's 14.7¢ flat price). The trade skips that charge unless it pays it.

facts.what: Demand response enrolled in the seven U.S. wholesale markets in 2024, and the share of their peak demand it could meet.
facts.source: FERC staff, 2025 Assessment of Demand Response and Advanced Metering, pp. 2, 14–15

facts.what: Demand response in the Southwest Power Pool market, Prairie Town's real-data home, in 2024, and its share of SPP's peak demand.
facts.source: FERC staff, 2025 Assessment of Demand Response and Advanced Metering, pp. 15–16

facts.what: FERC Order No. 2222 requires the regional grid operators it regulates to let aggregations of small resources into their markets, with a minimum size of no more than 100 kW.
